row-level security as the app role; cross-workspace ids through the API; roles; webhook routing

hold and undo, exactly-once send, provider failures, database-enforced order, audit log, approver routing (delegate to exec, CRM change to RevOps), approve and decline by id over the API, never-list, rules for unattended runs, demo-only actions refused
connect flow, backfill paging and resume, the nightly mail check, apps that cannot be connected yet, signed webhooks, duplicates, replies
blank workspace, commands, idempotent retry answered only to the sender, undo, ordering, stream, model setting, monthly limit and concurrent-run limit within the server's ceilings

Ask over mail, AG-UI stream, pause and resume, injected instructions, judge, credentials, switching the model (with a stand-in second model), cost log, caps including two jobs arriving at once, leases, drafting, reading new mail
calendar sync on connect, re-sync on a provider event, cancelled events, isolation

an event added in Timmy is created in Google Calendar after the undo window, once; guests are invited only after approval; Undo; an assistant's invitation waits for the exec; a guest with no address; no calendar connected; a refusal; a timeout confirmed from the calendar; the kill switch
one test per finding of the phase 0 safety review

one test per finding of the safety review of the first phase 1 additions: Auto mode tied to the open thread, the cap on filings per command, who a nudge may go to, when a nudge may be dropped, valid place names, two filings at once, a malformed action
cold email sends nothing through the provider; the compose link; sent and reply detection for leads through sync

one test per finding of the security audit: invite-only sign-up, workspaces per account, bounded chat input, the service-wide and unattended spending limits, leaving a workspace, two connects at once, deletion on disconnect and on workspace delete, request size limits, who may change rules, chat buttons and drafts, sender parsing, whose mailbox a send leaves from, browser headers, stream limit
the morning run: due by the workspace's own clock, once a day, drafts replies for what needs an answer, moves nothing and sends nothing, takes in missed mail first, stops at the spending limit

sorting or archiving a thread writes the label to the mailbox through an approved effect record; labels made once; Undo files it back; written once on a retried command; who may file; the kill switch; a refusal, a deleted label and a timeout; filing asked for in the chat waits for the person by default; Auto mode acts only on the open thread, and its judge sees only the person's words and a fixed description; an unattended run cannot file on its own

a draft that asks for something carries the item and a date; Send & track moves the thread to Waiting and labels it; the morning run drafts a nudge once the date passes; a nudge is never sent by itself; a reply ends the wait and drops the nudge

Timmy's own account mail through Resend: recorded first, delivered once with a fixed key, retried after a refusal, given up on when its link has expired, never delivered with stand-in providers on; the provider's key never logged; a new account can't sign in until its address is confirmed

Outlook through Composio: HTML bodies to text, folders to places, a forged display name never taken for an address; connect and the one-mailbox rule; first read, paging, new mail by event stored under the listing's id, a quoted conversation id can't change the query, the nightly check, hand-sent mail noticed; a new email sent once exactly as approved; a reply addressed to the approved people and not to whoever Outlook would answer; nothing sent when the draft's recipients don't match; timeouts found in Sent Items or left unconfirmed, never re-sent; filing as categories and the Archive folder, in batches of 20, finished after a partial refusal; disconnect removes the mail

Google Drive through Composio, read-only: connect beside a mailbox; the list of recent files without folders or trash; links kept only if they are Google's; paging, resuming, and asking only for what changed since; file events; the nightly pass; Ask's file search by name, wrapped as outside content; no other workspace sees the files; disconnect removes them

sign up, name the workspace, land on an empty Today with none of the demo's sample data, Approvals and Connections show the workspace's own state, sign out and in; a change survives an immediate reload; a save and a sign-out whose first attempt is lost on the way still happen, once
connect a mailbox, receive an email, see the thread, sorting it labels it in the mailbox, Timmy drafts a reply and it is approved and sent from Approvals, send with undo, reply, audit log
Ask over mail; a send proposed in chat needs the Send button; chat history is kept per person and removed at sign-out

the model picker (only tested models offered, an unlisted model refused), the monthly limit and its ceiling, the choice to let Timmy file mail itself. two workspaces in two browsers never see each other's data

a lead email opens Gmail's compose window signed by the signed-in person, nothing is sent through the provider, the lead is contacted once the email is in Sent, the reply shows in the Unibox
no run time is claimed without a mailbox; after the run Today says what it did, the drafted reply waits in Approvals, nothing is sent or moved

filing asked for in the chat shows the change and waits; with the setting on Timmy files the thread that is open, and still asks about any other; the audit log says which a person approved; an email still needs Send
connect Google Calendar; an event with a guest waits out the undo window, then is created with the guest invited, once, and shows once in Timmy; Undo means nobody is invited

in the browser: the Outlook card says what Timmy really reads; connect Outlook; Gmail refused beside it; an Outlook email arrives and reads as plain words; accepting a suggestion puts the category on it in Outlook; a drafted reply is approved, held, and sent once from the Outlook mailbox in the same conversation; archiving moves it to Outlook's Archive; connect Drive, a new file is announced, Ask finds it by name; disconnecting Outlook removes its thread

in the browser, on a server that requires address confirmation: a new account is told to confirm its address, is not signed in, can't get in with the password alone, and is signed in by opening the link sent to it
